extractions.quote: Our observation fulfils both the clinical as well as the electrophysiological criteria of SMS. In fact, the stiffness and rigidity began in axial muscles, slowly involving the proximal limb muscles; the painful spasms were triggered by sudden noise, movement or emotional upset; the neurological and intellective functions were normal; no abnormalities were disclosed by neuroradiological investigations [ 11]. EMG examination showed the constantly found electrophysiological counterpart of this syndrome, i.e. the spontaneous firing of motor unit action potentials involving antagonistic muscles

extractions.value: Needle EMG of antagonistic muscles at rest and during maximal effort; motor and sensory nerve conduction of four nerves (right median and peroneal, left ulnar and tibial); H reflex, H-M recruitment curve, H-H recovery curve; polysynaptic flexion reflexes RII and RIII of the short head of the biceps femoris and extension (RPPS) of the soleus; presynaptic inhibition index (vibration index); Ib soleus H reflex inhibition; Ia H reflex antagonistic inhibition; silent period in tibialis anterior during voluntary contraction stimulating the peroneal nerve.
